missing_pieces.duty: ED26-GAP-SCI-008-C04 (partial): Half of the success condition is met: the warranted assignment contrast is stated, with its weights and premises and the unbiasedness theorem (factorial-inference-and-estimability.tex 677-726, annex 373-392; 077 404-466), and no failure condition holds. The other half, 'the additional premise for a mechanism claim', is not stated. Lines 736-741 list only kinds of evidence: process measurements with an explicit measurement model, and interventions or controls that separate the competing mechanisms. They add an unspecified category, 'assumptions connecting those observations to the causal equations', and say only that a mechanism interpretation has 'its own premises'. The passages at 075 656-662 and 077 449-450 just point back to that paragraph. Nowhere on the route is the premise itself given, meaning what must be assumed before the estimable assignment contrast can support the reflection-mechanism claim. An example would be that the checking instruction affects the response only through the reflection variable, which rules out the effort pathway of model two in thm:p15-factorial-mechanism. Another would be a stated mediation premise. The chapter promises at lines 12-13 to state 'the additional conditions under which an estimable contrast is ... an identified causal mechanism', but it delivers only a theorem that the mechanism is not identified. The route also has no link to the mediation premises in handbook/parts/p16/causal-mediation.tex.

sections.title: Fractional factorial designs, aliasing and estimability

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-GAP-SCI-008-C04 (partial): The success condition requires stating the warranted assignment contrast and the additional premise for a mechanism claim. The first part is met: handbook/parts/p15/factorial-inference-and-estimability.tex 692-726 gives the weights (0,0,-1,1) and (-1,1,-1,1)/2 with the unbiased weighting estimator, and 077 404-466 lists the premises for the assignment contrast. The second part is not met. thm:p15-factorial-mechanism (728-734) proves that the factorial surface does not identify the reflection mechanism. The text then lists only kinds of further evidence plus unspecified 'assumptions connecting those observations to the causal equations' (736-741). The same deferral recurs without a premise at 077:449-450 ('needs the additional evidence'), 075:661-662 ('needs further premises again') and P19 evidence-methods.tex:667-670. No premise that would license a mechanism claim is ever stated. An example would be a structural restriction excluding the competing effort path that separates the theorem's two models, or a condition under which the reflection variable's intervention effect is identified. The chapter's own opening promise (lines 12-13) to state 'the additional conditions under which an estimable contrast is ... an identified causal mechanism' is therefore not delivered. The failure condition does not hold, because no coefficient is called proof of the mechanism.

required_components.description: Preserve the existing 2×2 design and derive main/interaction contrasts.
required_components.success_condition: Show conditional effects, average effects and the difference of differences with explicit coding.
required_components.failure_condition: Say factorial designs are absent or replace the existing valid opposite-sign example.

required_components.description: Explain replication, blocking and residual information.
required_components.success_condition: Demonstrate what repeated runs and blocked assignment add to estimation.
required_components.failure_condition: Confuse repeated measurements with independently assigned units.

required_components.description: Derive an alias in a fraction of a full factorial design.
required_components.success_condition: Show two design columns coincide and only their combined coefficient is identifiable.
required_components.failure_condition: Estimate aliased effects separately from the same deficient design.

required_components.description: Connect estimability to the causal claim.
required_components.success_condition: State the warranted assignment contrast and the additional premise for a mechanism claim.
required_components.failure_condition: Call a significant factorial coefficient proof of the proposed psychological mechanism.
